statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-34180 ("Heap Buffer Over-read in ASN.1 Content Parsing", Low): an integer truncation in OpenSSL's ASN.1 decoder mishandles the content length of a primitive element longer than 2 gigabytes, which can cause a heap buffer over-read on 64-bit Unix and Unix-like platforms in applications that pass attacker-supplied data to d2i_X509(), d2i_PKCS7() or another d2i_* decoding function; OpenSSL's command-line tools are not affected, because data read through the BIO layer is checked first. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.7; the FIPS modules are not affected because the code is outside the FIPS module boundary. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/da5d62af75f69d6fbf7803743d7c56ac75461e43, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.7. Alpine fixed it in openssl 3.5.7-r0 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-34180). The published DHI Alpine 3.23 builds from the openssl source (the main repository packages, and the openssl-fips FIPS-provider package in the DHI enterprise repository, built from the same source at matching versions from 3.5.5_git20260330-r1 on) are 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2, each on x86_64 and aarch64. The libcrypto in every one of these builds reports the OpenSSL release of its package version (3.5.5_git20260330-r1, a git snapshot dated 30 March 2026, reports 3.5.5). Builds before 3.5.7-r0 are based on OpenSSL 3.5.6 or earlier, and 3.5.7-r0 and every later build on OpenSSL 3.5.7 or later. The fix makes asn1_ex_c2i() reject a content length that does not fit in an int, raising ASN1_R_TOO_LONG (reason 155) at two new checks; the compiler inlines that function into asn1_d2i_ex_primitive(). Using that function's address from the shipped debug symbols, the disassembly of libcrypto shows two ERR_set_error() calls with reason 155 in that function in 3.5.7-r0 and every later build, and none in 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0 or 3.5.6-r1, on both architectures (debug symbols from the openssl-dbg package of each build). The openssl-fips package holds only the FIPS provider (fips.so, built from the same OpenSSL release as the package version in every build on both architectures) and its configuration files; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary.

CVE-2026-34180 ("Heap Buffer Over-read in ASN.1 Content Parsing", Low): an integer truncation in OpenSSL's ASN.1 decoder mishandles the content length of a primitive element longer than 2 gigabytes, which can cause a heap buffer over-read on 64-bit Unix and Unix-like platforms in applications that pass attacker-supplied data to d2i_X509(), d2i_PKCS7() or another d2i_* decoding function; OpenSSL's command-line tools are not affected, because data read through the BIO layer is checked first. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 (DSA-6335-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-34180). The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-34180. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 entry naming it. The fix makes asn1_ex_c2i() reject a content length that does not fit in an int, raising ASN1_R_TOO_LONG (reason 155) at two new checks; the compiler inlines that function into asn1_d2i_ex_primitive(). Using that function's address from the shipped debug symbols, the disassembly of libcrypto shows two ERR_set_error() calls with reason 155 in that function in every build from the first rebuild of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 on, FIPS builds included, and none in any earlier build, on both architectures (debug symbols from the libssl3t64-dbgsym package of each build). Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libcrypto and libssl are Debian's 3.5 libraries checked above.
